validity.recommendation: keep row; P7437 is the legitimate 114 km/26 in sibling, not a duplicate
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED. The Artawi (Ar-Ratawi) GMP EPSCC gas midstream pipeline package is real and well documented outside GEM: CPEC (China Petroleum Engineering Corp) announced in June 2025 that its subsidiary China Petroleum Pipeline Engineering (CPP) received a letter of award from TotalEnergies for the ~USD 294m / 36-month EPSCC covering a 114 km 26-in sour gas pipeline and an 83 km 20-in sour gas pipeline linking the Majnoon and West Qurna 2 oilfields to the new Artawi gas processing plant (Basra). Independently corroborated by MEED's own reporting (13 Jun 2025, client = TotalEnergies as GGIP operator, USD 294m) and by TotalEnergies' primary GGIP materials (GMP is a GGIP sub-project, commissioning scheduled 2028); Iraqi Ministry of Oil site-visit coverage (30 Jun 2026) confirms the Artawi project incl. the Majnoon/West Qurna 2/Artawi sourcing network is in active implementation. P7436 (83 km/20 in) = Pipeline 1; P7437 (114 km/26 in) = Pipeline 2 of the same award — siblings, not duplicates; no overlap with P6007 (West Qurna-Rumela, 50 km/40 in) or any other roster row. CAVEATS: (1) length/diameter ultimately trace to a single origin (the CPEC exchange announcement) relayed by many outlets, so specs are single-strong-source (medium) despite many reprints; (2) the English wire text (pipeline-journal/bcinsight, from Iraq Business News) garbles the scope by listing the '83-kilometre, 20-inch' line twice — the Chinese-language CPEC-derived text (aciep.net) gives exactly two lines (114 km/26 in + 83 km/20 in), matching GEM's two rows; the award also mentions three additional export pipelines + valve stations not captured as rows (possible future discovery item); (3) the sheet's current Status ref (pipeline-journal) does not contain the word 'proposed' and does not contain '2027', so Status and StartYear3 were unsupported by their own citation.

validity.recommendation: review PipelineType: sources describe a sour (raw associated) gas line from oilfields to a processing plant — 'gathering' per controlled vocab, not 'transmission'; reclassify or document the GGIT-inclusion rationale
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records PipelineType=transmission. Every independent source (CPEC announcement via aciep/bjx, pipeline-journal, bcinsight, MEED) describes these as MIDSTREAM SOUR GAS pipelines carrying raw associated gas FROM the Majnoon and West Qurna 2 oilfields TO the Artawi gas processing plant — i.e. upstream-of-processing feedstock/gathering service, not processed-gas transmission to market. GEM's controlled vocab has 'gathering' as a valid PipelineType. At 83 km/20 in it is large for a gathering line and GEM may deliberately include it in GGIT, but as recorded the type looks wrong; same issue applies to sibling P7437. Flagging rather than silently passing: reclassify to 'gathering' or add a ResearcherNotes divergence note.

validity.recommendation: review Owner: sheet says Iraq Ministry of Oil 100% (ref now bot-blocked, HTTP 401); the project is developed under the GGIP consortium — TotalEnergies 45% / Basrah Oil Company 30% / QatarEnergy 25%, TotalEnergies operator
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1=Iraq Ministry of Oil 100% is sourced only to iraq-businessnews.com, which now returns HTTP 401 (bot-verification wall) — the cited support is unverifiable. Independent sources say the EPSCC was awarded BY TotalEnergies as operator of the Gas Growth Integrated Project (GGIP), whose consortium is TotalEnergies 45%, Basrah Oil Company 30%, QatarEnergy 25% (TotalEnergies primary page + MEED independent reporting). Ministry of Oil as ultimate state asset owner is plausible under the GGIP contractual structure, but as recorded (100%, unverifiable ref) it conflicts with how every reachable source attributes the project. Recommend Baird decide: record GGIP consortium as owner (with TotalEnergies as Operator, currently blank) or keep MoO with a documented-divergence note and a working ref.

validity.recommendation: start year: 2027 (StartYear3) is unsupported by its cited ref; TotalEnergies puts GMP commissioning at 2028 — consider 2027 -> 2028
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet has StartYear3=2027 with the pipeline-journal article as ref, but that article contains no 2027 (verifier: value not found) — it says 36 months from the June 2025 award, i.e. ~mid-2028. TotalEnergies' GGIP page (primary) states GMP commissioning is 'scheduled in 2028'; bcinsight (CRU) also reports GMP commissioning 2028. The only 2027 trace is MEED's June 2025 line that TotalEnergies 'aims for full operational readiness by 2027', which the operator's own later materials supersede. Length 83 km and diameter 20 in are CONFIRMED as-recorded (pipeline-journal + Chinese CPEC-derived aciep.net agree; note both trace to the CPEC announcement, so treat as one strong origin). Capacity is blank in the sheet and correctly so: the 300 MMcf/d (phase 1) / 600 MMcf/d figures are GMP plant capacity, never stated per-pipeline — do not backfill.

fills.researcher_notes: ConstructionYear=2025 was in the sheet with no ref. TotalEnergies press release (15 Sep 2025): 'the 300 Mcf/d Gas Midstream Project (GMP), whose construction began early 2025'. Caveat: that statement covers the GMP umbrella (plant + network); the pipeline EPSCC itself was only awarded to CPP in June 2025, so pipe-spread construction start could be later — medium tier, single primary origin for the 2025 date.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Recorded 'proposed' (LastUpdated 2025-07-16) is stale and was already internally inconsistent (ConstructionYear=2025 filled; Status ref does not contain 'proposed'). Newer dated evidence: (1) TotalEnergies press release 15 Sep 2025 — 'the 300 Mcf/d Gas Midstream Project (GMP), whose construction began early 2025' (primary, operator); (2) Iraqi Ministry of Oil site visit reported 30 Jun 2026 (oilandgasadvancement.com) — deputy oil minister toured ongoing construction at Artawi, project 'entered a critical deployment phase', GMP progress inspected, with the Majnoon/West Qurna 2/Artawi sourcing network as a named component. Two independent origins (operator + government) put the GMP in active construction through June 2026, and the pipeline EPSCC (CPP, USD 294m, 36 months) was awarded June 2025 targeting the 2028 GMP commissioning. CAVEAT kept at medium: neither source names the two pipeline spreads specifically as under construction (no weld/groundbreak item found in EN/AR/ZH searches — searched 'Artawi/Ratawi pipeline construction', 'CPP 管道局 阿塔维 开工/焊接', Arabic 'الرطاوي مجنون غرب القرنة'); the construction evidence is at GMP-project level. Sibling GGIT rows for the same complex (e.g. P7434, P6007) are already 'construction'. If Baird prefers strict pipe-level evidence, keep 'proposed' with the 2026-06 activity note — but 'proposed' no longer reflects the project state.

summary: P7436 real (CPEC/CPP USD294m EPSCC for TotalEnergies GGIP; 83km/20in confirmed); status proposed -> construction (TotalEnergies 2025-09 + MoO 2026-06); concerns: PipelineType likely gathering not transmission (sour gas field-to-plant), Owner MoO-100% unverifiable vs GGIP consortium, StartYear 2027 unsupported vs 2028.
